Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Your Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is simply to listen and understand how life has felt for you since your baby arrived. We’ll be using a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS. It helps us pick up on signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up in the first year postpartum, and it includes one question about self-harm so we can make sure you’re safe. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might hurt yourself or your baby, and then we’d talk together about extra support. There are only ten questions, and I’ll ask each one conversationally—no numbers or check-boxes on your end. Just answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to begin?

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I’ve still managed to laugh a little—maybe once or twice when my partner made a silly joke while we were changing diapers—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Things that would have cracked me up before now might just make me smile, and sometimes I feel like I’m faking it more than really feeling it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, but not as much as I used to. Most days something small will still make me chuckle—like when the baby makes those funny milk-drunk faces—but the laughter feels kind of quick and fades fast. I guess I’d say not as often or as strongly as before she was born.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like taking the baby for a short walk around the block or having my morning coffee—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. Before she was born, I’d really anticipate meeting friends or going out to eat, and now those plans feel like more effort than fun.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. When she won’t settle at night, I immediately think I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m holding her weird or didn’t burp her long enough. Rationally I know babies just fuss, but the thought still pops in that I’m not a good-enough mom. It’s not constant, but a couple of times this week I’ve ended up in tears because I felt like I was failing her.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Every now and then my mind just races—like I’ll suddenly wonder if her breathing sounds different or if she’s getting enough milk. There’s not always a clear trigger. I can usually calm myself down pretty quickly, but those random waves of worry pop up a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had any real panic attacks, but sometimes I’ll get this sudden flutter of fear—like I’m standing at the top of a staircase and the world tilts for a second. It’s brief, maybe a minute or two, and then I’m okay. Nothing specific sets it off; it just shows up and passes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. When she’s fussy and the laundry’s piling up, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually get through it—if my partner walks in or I put her in the sling, I can breathe again—but that overwhelmed feeling creeps in most afternoons.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve had a couple of nights where it took me an extra half-hour to nod off because my head was spinning with little worries, but once I’m asleep I stay out until she wakes for a feed. So my sleep’s mostly okay—just the odd rocky start.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I do feel that way some of the time. Not all day, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon—when I just feel really low, like I could cry. It’s happened maybe three or four days this week, and it usually lifts after an hour or so, but while it’s there I feel pretty heavy and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when she wouldn’t latch and once when I dropped a plate and it shattered. The tears don’t last long, maybe ten minutes, but yeah, the littlest thing sets me off and I feel like I’m leaking from every part of me.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired and weepy, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that—nothing about wanting to hurt myself at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]  

A. Positive findings (frequency, severity)  
- Persistent low mood: “heavy and weepy” most late-afternoons, 3–4 days/week  
- Anhedonia: diminished laughter/anticipation; activities “more effort than fun”  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt: multiple times/week (“not a good-enough mom”)  
- Generalized anxiety: racing worries 2–3× daily, no clear trigger  
- Brief panicky surges: 1–2 min episodes, several/week  
- Overwhelm / difficulty coping: near-daily afternoon episodes, relieved by support  
- Crying spells: twice this week, precipitated by minor events  
- Mild initial insomnia: occasional 30-min delay, no middle/terminal insomnia  

B. Protective / negative findings  
- Denies any self-harm ideation  
- Sleep architecture largely preserved once asleep  
- Episodes remit with support or distraction  
- No anhedonia absolute—still finds small enjoyments (walks, coffee)  

C. Screening significance  
Findings cross threshold for probable mild–moderate postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety; no current safety risk.  

D. Recommendations  
Continue monitoring; consider formal EPDS and clinical interview for diagnostic clarification and treatment planning.
